```text
1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
5	\label{sec:formulation}
6	
7	We formulate per-head KV cache quantization as a constrained optimization problem.
8	Let $h \in \{1,\ldots,H\}$ index the KV heads across all layers, $b_h \in \mathcal{B}$ the bit-width assigned to head $h$, and $\mathcal{B} = \{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ the set of hardware-aligned bit-widths.
9	Each head $h$ has a profiled distortion function $d_h(b)$, the PPL increase when head $h$ is quantized to $b$ bits.
10	Given a memory budget ratio $R$ (e.g., $R = 0.25$ for $4\times$ compression), we seek the allocation that minimizes total distortion:
11	\begin{equation}
12	\label{eq:objective}
13	\min_{\{b_h\}} \sum_{h=1}^{H} d_h(b_h) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \frac{1}{H \cdot 16}\sum_{h=1}^{H} b_h \leq R.
14	\end{equation}
15	
16	This is a multiple-choice knapsack problem (MCKP): each head selects one bit-width from $\mathcal{B}$ to minimize total distortion under a budget.
17	RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} solves this for consecutive bit-widths $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, where the polymatroid structure of the feasible set guarantees that greedy allocation is optimal (their Proposition 6).
18	Hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ are non-consecutive; the gaps break this structure, and greedy is no longer guaranteed to match the MCKP optimum.
19	Moreover, as we show in \S\ref{sec:compounding}, the objective itself is not well-behaved: distortions from 2-bit heads compound non-additively, making unconstrained optimization unreliable.
20	
21	\subsection{PPL-based Per-Head Profiling}
22	\label{sec:profiling}
23	
24	We use symmetric per-channel quantization with per-head granularity: each KV head is independently quantized to one of the candidate bit-widths $\mathcal{B} = \{2, 4, 8, 16\}$, without per-token scaling.
25	We profile each head by quantizing it to each $b \in \mathcal{B}$ while keeping all other heads at bf16, and measuring the resulting PPL increase $d_h(b)$ on a calibration set of 64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train.
26	This yields a distortion table of $H \times |\mathcal{B}|$ entries that serves as input to the solver.
27	
28	The optimization in Eq.~\eqref{eq:objective} relies on an additive distortion assumption: the total PPL degradation from a mixed-precision allocation is approximately $\sum_h d_h(b_h)$.
29	This holds when per-head distortions are small and independent---a reasonable approximation for 4-bit and 8-bit quantization, where individual head distortions are typically below 0.1 PPL.
30	At 2-bit, however, individual distortions are orders of magnitude larger, and the additive assumption breaks down.
31	
32	\subsection{Compounding Effect}
33	\label{sec:compounding}
34	
35	When many heads are simultaneously quantized to 2-bit, per-head distortions compound non-additively: truncation errors from multiple 2-bit heads accumulate through the residual stream, and once their count exceeds the network's capacity to compensate, PPL degrades super-linearly.
36	
37	Unconstrained solvers are blind to this effect because the additive objective underestimates the cost of large-scale 2-bit assignment.
38	On Qwen2.5-7B, unconstrained greedy assigns 68 heads to 2-bit and achieves 32.45 PPL; unconstrained MCKP assigns 75 heads and achieves 36.92---both far worse than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
39	Standard-resolution profiling detects non-zero $d_h(2)$ for only 37 of 112 heads; the remaining 75 heads have $d_h(2) \approx 0$, so most 2-bit assignments appear free to the additive objective.
40	The resulting additive prediction is $\sum_h d_h(b_h) + \text{baseline} \approx 11$ PPL---$3\text{--}4\times$ lower than the actual 32--37 PPL, because the compounding interaction between simultaneously quantized heads is invisible to per-head profiling.
41	
42	This compounding is specific to 2-bit quantization and is \emph{super-additive}: quantizing the top-$k$ most sensitive heads to 2-bit simultaneously produces PPL $1.56\times$ the sum of their individual distortions at $k{=}8$, growing to $4.89\times$ at $k{=}64$.
43	A random-$k$ control confirms that sensitivity ordering matters: at $k{=}64$, random selection yields 55.94 PPL vs.\ 22.95 for top-$k$, because random draws are more likely to include high-distortion heads that amplify compounding.
44	At 4-bit and above, per-head distortions are small enough that additivity holds even when all heads share the same bit-width (uniform 4-bit achieves 15.45 PPL, close to the sum-of-distortions prediction).
45	The qualitative difference arises because 2-bit quantization has far larger per-head distortion, saturating the error tolerance of the residual stream.
46	
47	The relationship between $k$ and PPL is U-shaped (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}, Appendix~\ref{sec:compounding_appendix}): at $k{=}0$ (uniform 4-bit), PPL is 15.45; allowing a few 2-bit heads reduces PPL by freeing budget for 8-bit heads on sensitive positions, reaching a minimum of 11.23 at $k{=}8$; beyond $k{=}8$, compounding drives PPL upward.
48	
49	\subsection{Cardinality Constraint}
50	\label{sec:cardinality}
51	
52	The compounding effect motivates a simple addition to Eq.~\eqref{eq:objective}: a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments.
53	\begin{equation}
54	\label{eq:constraint}
55	\sum_{h=1}^{H} \mathbb{1}[b_h = 2] \leq k.
56	\end{equation}
57	
58	The constraint parameter $k$ is selected by a small-scale sweep on calibration data: solve the constrained problem for each candidate $k$, evaluate calibration PPL, and pick the value at the minimum of the U-shaped curve (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}).
59	For Qwen2.5-7B with 112 KV heads, $k{=}8$ ($\sim$7\% of heads).
60	
61	The constraint is a single linear inequality, compatible with any solver---greedy, MCKP, or integer linear programming---and adds negligible overhead to the optimization.
62	
63	One might expect Layer-0 heads to require explicit protection.
64	On Qwen2.5-7B, however, the profiler assigns very high 2-bit distortion to Layer-0 heads (L0H0: $+$31.9\%, L0H2: $+$23.2\%, L0H3: $+$11.7\% relative to bf16), so no solver would assign them 2-bit under any reasonable budget.
65	Running the solver with and without manual Layer-0 exclusion produces identical allocations; no manual rule is needed.
66	
67	\paragraph{Restoring additivity.}
68	The additive objective treats per-head distortions as independent, but 2-bit compounding violates this once many 2-bit heads coexist.
69	Restricting 2-bit heads to $k \ll H$ pushes the allocation back into a near-additive regime where the profiler's prediction agrees with measured PPL.
70	For Qwen2.5-7B, $k{=}8$ ($\sim$7\% of heads) is few enough that compounding contributes negligibly, consistent with the U-shaped curve minimum (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}).
71	This explains the constrained--unconstrained gap in Table~\ref{tab:solver_equiv}: constrained greedy operates inside the additive regime (11.23 PPL, matching the ${\approx}11$ additive estimate), while unconstrained solvers extrapolate outside it and miss true PPL by $3\text{--}4\times$.
72	
73	\subsection{Solver Equivalence}
74	\label{sec:solver_equiv}
75	
76	\begin{table}[t]
77	\centering
78	\small
79	\caption{Solver comparison on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression. Unconstrained solvers over-allocate 2-bit heads and fail catastrophically. The cardinality constraint ($k{\leq}8$) makes greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations.\protect\footnotemark}
80	\label{tab:solver_equiv}
81	\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
82	\toprule
83	Solver & Constraint & PPL & \multicolumn{3}{c}{Bit distribution} \\
84	 & & & 2-bit & 4-bit & 8/16-bit \\
85	\midrule
86	Greedy & None & 32.45 & 68 & 30 & 14 \\
87	MCKP & None & 36.92 & 75 & 33 & 4 \\
88	Greedy & $k{\leq}8$ & 11.23 & 8 & 100 & 4 \\
89	MCKP & $k{\leq}8$ & 11.23 & 8 & 100 & 4 \\
90	Uniform & --- & 15.45 & 0 & 112 & 0 \\
91	\bottomrule
92	\end{tabular}
93	\end{table}
94	\footnotetext{Standard-resolution profiling for illustration; main results (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) use high-resolution profiling (10.91 PPL).}
95	
96	With the cardinality constraint, greedy and MCKP produce identical results (Table~\ref{tab:solver_equiv}): same PPL (11.23), same bit distribution on Qwen2.5-7B.
97	
98	\paragraph{Empirical observation.}
99	When $k \ll H$ and the top-$k$ heads ranked by marginal benefit $d_h(4) - d_h(2)$ contain no ties, constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical per-head allocations.
100	The constraint restricts the feasible set so that the only decision is which $k$ heads to assign 2-bit; the marginal-benefit ordering determines this uniquely, so greedy's local choice coincides with the global optimum.
101	We verify this across three architectures: Qwen2.5-7B (112/112 heads identical), Llama-3.1-8B (256/256), Mistral-7B-v0.3 (255/256; the single difference is a zero-distortion tie with no PPL impact).
102	Without the constraint, greedy cascades into excessive 2-bit allocation, as each additional 2-bit head looks locally beneficial but contributes to compounding.
103	Practitioners can therefore use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm without sacrificing optimality.
104	
105	A per-layer brute-force oracle on Qwen2.5-7B confirms near-optimality: of 8 layers with non-trivial allocations, MCKP matches the oracle on 5; the remaining 3 have a maximum gap of 0.018 PPL (0.4\% of the total improvement), closing the optimality chain from greedy through MCKP to brute-force.

no manual rule is needed.\n\n\\paragraph{Restoring additivity.}\nThe additive objective treats per-head distortions as independent, but 2-bit compounding violates this once many 2-bit heads coexist.\nRestricting 2-bit heads to $k \\ll H$ pushes the allocation back into a near-additive regime where the profiler's prediction agrees with measured PPL.\nFor Qwen2.5-7B, $k{=}8$ ($\\sim$7\\% of heads) is few enough that compounding contributes negligibly, consistent with the U-shaped curve minimum (Figure~\\ref{fig:compounding}).\nThis explains the constrained--unconstrained gap in Table~\\ref{tab:solver_equiv}: constrained greedy operates inside the additive regime (11.23 PPL, matching the ${\\approx}11$ additive estimate), while unconstrained solvers extrapolate outside it and miss true PPL by $3\\text{--}4\\times$.\n\n\\subsection{Solver Equivalence}\n\\label{sec:solver_equiv}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Solver comparison on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\\times$ compression. Unconstrained solvers over-allocate 2-bit heads and fail catastrophically. 1	Non-uniform per-head KV cache quantization helps only when head sensitivity exhibits a specific distribution shape---a finding obscured by prior work's focus on aggregate metrics.
2	We study seven models spanning 1.4B--14B parameters and five architecture families (MHA through GQA 8:1) on hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ and find that the benefit of per-head allocation depends not on GQA ratio or overall sensitivity magnitude, but on whether heterogeneity is \emph{spread} across multiple heads with cross-bitwidth gradients or concentrated in a single outlier.
3	On the one spread-pattern model (Qwen2.5-7B), a cardinality-constrained solver achieves 10.91 perplexity at $4\times$ compression---a 29.4\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45)---while unconstrained solvers fail catastrophically (32--37 PPL) due to 2-bit distortion compounding through the residual stream.
4	On the remaining six models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where scaling dilutes spread into flat---non-uniform allocation provides no meaningful benefit: Yi-1.5-9B has the highest concentration tested (0.71, exceeding Qwen-7B's 0.61) yet gains nothing, because its heterogeneity is a single-outlier ``spike'' with no cross-bitwidth gradient.
5	The cardinality constraint prevents catastrophic failure on spread architectures, moderate over-allocation on flat architectures (Gemma-2: unconstrained $1.47\times$ degradation reduced to within 0.5\% of uniform), and renders solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations---enabling a simple $O(H\log H)$ greedy algorithm.
6	We propose a joint empirical decision rule combining concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio) that correctly classifies all seven evaluated models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\ 14B flat).

```text
1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Per-head mixed-precision quantization of the KV cache is a natural strategy for reducing memory during LLM inference: assign fewer bits to insensitive heads and more bits to sensitive ones, achieving lower perplexity than uniform quantization at the same average bit-width.
5	Recent work on KV cache quantization explores both uniform schemes~\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant,lin2024qserve,he2024zipcache} and token-level mixed-precision approaches~\cite{ge2024fastgen,lei2026arkv}, while complementary methods reduce cache size through eviction~\cite{zhang2023h2o,li2024snapkv}.
6	RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalizes per-head allocation as a rate-distortion optimization and shows that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).
7	
8	In practice, hardware-efficient inference requires bit-widths drawn from $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$---the formats natively supported by modern accelerators.
9	On this non-consecutive set, the polymatroid structure breaks down, and greedy is no longer provably optimal.
10	One might expect that exact MCKP solvers would fill this gap.
11	They do not.
12	On Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression, unconstrained greedy achieves 32.45 PPL and unconstrained MCKP achieves 36.92---both \emph{far worse} than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
13	The optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.
14	
15	The root cause is not solver suboptimality but a violation of the additive distortion assumption.
16	Both solvers assign 68--75 of 112 KV heads to 2-bit, where per-head quantization errors compound through the residual stream.
17	The additive model predicts $\sim$11 PPL; the actual PPL is $3$--$4\times$ higher, because 2-bit distortions are orders of magnitude larger than 4-bit and compound super-linearly when many heads are quantized simultaneously.
18	
19	This observation points to a minimal intervention: cap the number of 2-bit assignments.
20	We add a single cardinality constraint $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h{=}2] \leq k$ to the standard MCKP formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}).
21	On Qwen2.5-7B, setting $k{=}8$ (7\% of heads) yields 10.91 PPL---a 29.4\% reduction over uniform 4-bit.
22	The constraint works by forcing the solver to use 2-bit only on the least-sensitive heads, while redistributing the freed budget to protect sensitive heads at 8-bit or 16-bit.
23	This is not a heuristic patch: the constraint directly addresses the identified failure mode and is compatible with any solver.
24	The constraint is beneficial even on flat-distribution architectures: on Gemma-2-9B, unconstrained MCKP assigns 31.5\% of heads to 2-bit, producing a moderate $1.47\times$ degradation; the constraint reduces this to within 0.5\% of uniform.
25	
26	A surprising consequence is that the cardinality constraint renders solver choice irrelevant.
27	Constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations across all tested architectures (112/112 heads on Qwen, 256/256 on Llama, 255/256 on Mistral), enabling practitioners to use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm.
28	A per-layer brute-force oracle confirms near-optimality: the maximum gap is 0.02 PPL, 0.4\% of the total improvement (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).
29	
30	However, non-uniform allocation does not help universally.
31	On the remaining six models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where the $3.4\times$ increase in head count dilutes spread into flat---constrained MCKP provides no meaningful improvement.
32	The difference traces to the \emph{distribution shape} of head sensitivity, not GQA ratio or model scale alone: Qwen-7B's Layer-0 heads form a cluster of high sensitivity across multiple bitwidths (``spread''); Yi-1.5 and Llama have dominant outliers (``spike''); Gemma-2, Mistral, Qwen-14B, and Pythia show near-uniform or diluted sensitivity (``flat'').
33	
34	This motivates a question prior work does not address: \emph{when} should a practitioner use per-head mixed-precision quantization?
35	We propose a joint empirical decision rule based on concentration and distribution shape (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) that correctly classifies all seven evaluated models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast.
36	Yi-1.5 is a critical test: its concentration ($0.71$) exceeds Qwen-7B's, but its single-outlier spike has no cross-bitwidth gradient, so MCKP cannot redistribute budget.
37	
38	Our contributions are:
39	\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
40	\item We identify 2-bit distortion compounding as the cause of catastrophic failure in unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths, and show that a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments is a minimal sufficient fix, reducing Qwen2.5-7B PPL from 32--37 (unconstrained) to 10.91 (constrained) at $4\times$ compression (\S\ref{sec:compounding}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}).
41	
42	\item We demonstrate that the cardinality constraint serves three roles: preventing catastrophic failure on spread architectures (Qwen: 32.45$\to$10.91), preventing moderate over-allocation on flat architectures (Gemma-2: 8.85$\to$within 0.5\% of uniform), and rendering solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce equivalent allocations across all tested architectures (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).
43

Yi-1.5-9B serves as a critical test: its concentration exceeds Qwen-7B's, yet its single-outlier spike pattern means MCKP provides no benefit over uniform (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).

      "content": "\\section{Introduction}\n\\label{sec:introduction}\n\nPer-head mixed-precision quantization of the KV cache is a natural strategy for reducing memory during LLM inference: assign fewer bits to insensitive heads and more bits to sensitive ones, achieving lower perplexity than uniform quantization at the same average bit-width.\nRecent work on KV cache quantization explores both uniform schemes~\\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant,lin2024qserve,he2024zipcache} and token-level mixed-precision approaches~\\cite{ge2024fastgen,lei2026arkv}, while complementary methods reduce cache size through eviction~\\cite{zhang2023h2o,li2024snapkv}.\nRateQuant~\\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalizes per-head allocation as a rate-distortion optimization and shows that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\\{2,3,4,5,6\\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).\n\nIn practice, hardware-efficient inference requires bit-widths drawn from $\\{2, 4, 8, 16\\}$---the formats natively supported by modern accelerators.\nOn this non-consecutive set, the polymatroid structure breaks down, and greedy is no longer provably optimal.\nOne might expect that exact MCKP solvers would fill this gap.\nThey do not.\nOn Qwen2.5-7B at $4\\times$ compression, unconstrained greedy achieves 32.45 PPL and unconstrained MCKP achieves 36.92---both \\emph{far worse} than uniform 4-bit (15.45).\nThe optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.\n\nThe root cause is not solver suboptimality but a violation of the additive distortion assumption.\nBoth solvers assign 68--75 of 112 KV heads to 2-bit, where per-head quantization errors compound through the residual stream.\nThe additive model predicts $\\sim$11 PPL; the actual PPL is $3$--$4\\times$ higher, because 2-bit distortions are orders of magnitude larger than 4-bit and compound super-linearly when many heads are quantized simultaneously.\n\nThis observation points to a minimal intervention: cap the number of 2-bit assignments.\nWe add a single cardinality constraint $\\sum_h \\mathbb{1}[b_h{=}2] \\leq k$ to the standard MCKP formulation (\\S\\ref{sec:method}).\nOn Qwen2.5-7B, setting $k{=}8$ (7\\% of heads) yields 10.91 PPL---a 29.4\\% reduction over uniform 4-bit.\nThe constraint works by forcing the solver to use 2-bit only on the least-sensitive heads, while redistributing the freed budget to protect sensitive heads at 8-bit or 16-bit.\nThis is not a heuristic patch: the constraint directly addresses the identified failure mode and is compatible with any solver.\nThe constraint is beneficial even on flat-distribution architectures: on Gemma-2-9B, unconstrained MCKP assigns 31.5\\% of heads to 2-bit, producing a moderate $1.47\\times$ degradation; the constraint reduces this to within 0.5\\% of uniform.\n\nA surprising consequence is that the cardinality constraint renders solver choice irrelevant.\nConstrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations across all tested architectures (112/112 heads on Qwen, 256/256 on Llama, 255/256 on Mistral), enabling practitioners to use the simpler $O(H \\log H)$ greedy algorithm.\nA per-layer brute-force oracle confirms near-optimality: the maximum gap is 0.02 PPL, 0.4\\% of the total improvement (\\S\\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).\n\nHowever, non-uniform allocation does not help universally.\nOn the remaining six models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where the $3.4\\times$ increase in head count dilutes spread into flat---constrained MCKP provides no meaningful improvement.\nThe difference traces to the \\emph{distribution shape} of head sensitivity, not GQA ratio or model scale alone: Qwen-7B's Layer-0 heads form a cluster of high sensitivity across multiple bitwidths (``spread''); Yi-1.5 and Llama have dominant outliers (``spike''); Gemma-2, Mistral, Qwen-14B, and Pythia show near-uniform or diluted sensitivity (``flat'').\n\nThis motivates a question prior work does not address: \\emph{when} should a practitioner use per-head mixed-precision quantization?\nWe propose a joint empirical decision rule based on concentration and distribution shape (\\S\\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) that correctly classifies all seven evaluated models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast.\nYi-1.5 is a critical test: its concentration ($0.71$) exceeds Qwen-7B's, but its single-outlier spike has no cross-bitwidth gradient, so MCKP cannot redistribute budget.\n\nOur contributions are:\n\\begin{enumerate}[nosep]\n\\item We identify 2-bit distortion compounding as the cause of catastrophic failure in unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths, and show that a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments is a minimal sufficient fix, reducing Qwen2.5-7B PPL from 32--37 (unconstrained) to 10.91 (constrained) at $4\\times$ compression (\\S\\ref{sec:compounding}, \\S\\ref{sec:experiments}).\n\n\\item We demonstrate that the cardinality constraint serves three roles: preventing catastrophic failure on spread architectures (Qwen: 32.45$\\to$10.91), preventing moderate over-allocation on flat architectures (Gemma-2: 8.85$\\to$within 0.5\\% of uniform), and rendering solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce equivalent allocations across all tested architectures (\\S\\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).\n\n\\item We propose a joint empirical decision rule combining concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio) that correctly classifies all seven evaluated models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\\ 14B flat). Yi-1.5-9B serves as a critical test: its concentration exceeds Qwen-7B's, yet its single-outlier spike pattern means MCKP provides no benefit over uniform (\\S\\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).\n\\end{enumerate}\n",

60	This motivates a joint empirical decision rule for deciding when non-uniform allocation is worthwhile.

63	\item \textbf{Spread} (concentration $\gtrsim 0.50$, $t_1/t_5 \lesssim 0.70$): non-uniform recommended. Qwen (0.61, $t_1/t_5{=}0.57$): $-$29.4\% PPL.
64	\item \textbf{Spike} ($t_1/t_5 \gtrsim 0.70$, concentration $\gtrsim 0.25$): use uniform. A dominant outlier with no cross-bitwidth gradient cannot be exploited. Yi-1.5 (0.71, 0.90) and Llama (0.57, 0.85): no benefit.
65	\item \textbf{Flat} (concentration $\lesssim 0.25$, or remaining moderate-concentration models with $t_1/t_5 \lesssim 0.70$): use uniform. Too little cumulative delta for meaningful reallocation. Mistral (0.24), Gemma-2 (0.23), Qwen-14B (0.33), and Pythia (0.24): no benefit or counterproductive.
66	\end{itemize}

1	\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	Per-head mixed-precision KV cache quantization over hardware-aligned bit-widths \{2, 4, 8, 16\} requires a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments to prevent non-additive distortion compounding.
4	On Qwen2.5-7B, limiting 2-bit heads to $k{\leq}8$ reduces PPL from 15.45 (uniform 4-bit) to 10.91 ($-$29.4\%) at $4\times$ compression, while making solver choice irrelevant: constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations across all tested architectures.
5	Whether non-uniform allocation helps depends on the \emph{shape} of head sensitivity heterogeneity---spread patterns (Qwen-7B, $t_1/t_5{=}0.57$) yield large gains, while spike (Yi-1.5, Llama) and flat (Mistral, Gemma-2, Qwen-14B, Pythia) patterns show no benefit.
6	A joint empirical decision rule based on concentration and $t_1/t_5$ ratio correctly classifies all seven evaluated models (7/7), including a within-family scale contrast where Qwen-14B's spread dilutes into flat.
7	Extending to 70B+ models, production inference engines, and per-side K/V cardinality constraints (Appendix~\ref{sec:kv_separation}) are natural next steps.
8	
9	\section*{Limitations}
10	
11	Spread rests on $N{=}1$ (Qwen2.5-7B); the seven-model evaluation is directional, not robust. No real-kernel latency benchmarks; untested beyond 14B.
12	
```

  "text": "## 交叉回应 — Reviewer 1 对 Reviewer 2 审稿意见的逐条回应\n\n---\n\n### Weaknesses 回应\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W1: Abstract \"29.4% reduction\" 突出呈现具有误导性**\n\n同意核心判断，但需指出 abstract 已有一定限定。Abstract 第 3 行写 \"On the one spread-pattern model (Qwen2.5-7B)\"，第 4 行立即转向 \"On the remaining six models... non-uniform allocation provides no meaningful benefit\"。结构上做到了正反兼顾。\n\n但 R2 的核心关切成立：29.4% 是整篇论文最显眼的定量数据，且出现在 abstract 第 3 句——大部分读者首先记住的就是这个数字。\"one spread-pattern model\" 的限定语容易被略过。建议在 abstract 开头就明确 \"6/7 models show no benefit\" 的结论，再给 29.4% 作为唯一例外的说明，而非当前的先正后负叙述顺序。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W2: 经验判别规则的实用价值存疑——profiling 后直接跑 solver 即可**\n\n这是 R2 最锐利的观察之一，我在 Round 2 审稿中未充分展开。\n\n论文 Section 5.2（analysis.tex 第 72 行）自己写道：\"The rule reuses profiling data already required by the solver and adds no overhead.\" 这句话实际上暴露了问题：如果 decision rule 的输入（per-head profiling）与 solver 的输入完全相同，而 solver 运行时间是 O(H log H) 微秒级（Section 3.5），那么判别规则的唯一实用场景是\"不想跑 solver\"——但这在工程上没有理由，因为 solver 比 profiling 快几个数量级。\n\n判别规则的真实价值是**解释性**而非决策性：它回答了\"为什么有些模型获益而有些不获益\"这个科学问题。但论文将其定位为 contribution 3（introduction.tex 第 44 行），暗示了实用决策功能。建议将 decision rule 的定位从\"practical diagnostic tool\"降为\"post-hoc analytical framework for understanding when non-uniform allocation helps\"。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE，有保留] R2-W3: 与 RateQuant 的增量贡献界定模糊**\n\nR2 说\"技术上归结为 RateQuant + 一条 cardinality constraint\"基本正确，但略有低估。\n\n论文 method.tex 第 6-7、17 行明确陈述了与 RateQuant 的关系：RateQuant 处理 consecutive bit-widths {2,3,4,5,6}，利用 polymatroid structure 保证 greedy 最优；本文处理 hardware-aligned {2,4,8,16}，polymatroid structure 不成立。这是一个有意义的实践差异——实际部署确实使用 {2,4,8,16} 而非 {2,3,4,5,6}。\n\n但算法层面的增量确实很薄：MCKP formulation 相同，仅加一条 linear inequality。论文的真正贡献在于：(a) compounding effect 的系统性刻画（Section 3.3），(b) 7 个模型的 \"mostly negative\" 实证发现，(c) 异质性 characterization。这些分析性贡献比算法贡献更重要，但论文的叙事重心偏向了算法。\n\n建议作者更诚实地定位：**核心贡献是实证发现和分析框架，算法改进是自然推论。**\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W4: \"Catastrophic failure\" 叙事过度渲染**\n\n同意。核查原文：\n\n- Introduction 第 13 行：\"The optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.\"——特指 Qwen2.5-7B（32-37 PPL）\n- 但 abstract 第 5 行：\"prevents catastrophic failure on spread architectures\"——复数形式暗示 spread 不止一个，而实际只有 Qwen2.5-7B\n- Introduction contribution 1：\"catastrophic failure in unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization\"——措辞上没有限定为单一模型\n\nR2 正确指出：对其他模型，unconstrained solver 的退化是 \"moderate\"（Gemma-2: 1.47× degradation, intro 第 24 行），而非 \"catastrophic\"。将 moderate degradation 纳入 \"catastrophic failure\" 的叙事框架是过度渲染。这与我在 R1-W2 中关于 \"cause\" 措辞过强的观察一致。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W5: Spread/spike/flat 术语缺乏 formal definition**\n\n同意。Section 5.2（analysis.tex 第 63-66 行）使用 soft boundaries（\"$\\gtrsim 0.50$\", \"$\\lesssim 0.70$\"），三种 pattern 的边界条件存在重叠区域（如 concentration 0.33 + t1/t5 0.68 的 Qwen-14B 被归为 flat，但理由是 concentration 不够高，而非 shape）。Flat 的定义尤其模糊——既包括低 concentration（Mistral 0.24）也包括中等 concentration + 低 t1/t5（Qwen-14B 0.33, 0.68）。\n\nminor 问题，但对可复现性有影响。建议至少用 crisp inequality 定义（即便承认阈值是 empirical）。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W6: Related work 对 token-level mixed-precision 定位可更精确**\n\n同意。Introduction 第 5 行将 FastGen 和 ARKV 归为 \"token-level mixed-precision approaches\"，但未区分 token-level（每个 token 不同精度）和 head-level（每个 head 不同精度）方法的根本差异——前者的搜索空间是 O(T×H)，后者是 O(H)。对于一篇以 per-head allocation 为核心的论文，这个区分应该更清晰。\n\nMinor 问题。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W7: Limitations section 过于简短**\n\n强烈同意。Conclusion.tex 第 9-11 行的 Limitations 全文仅一句话：\n\n> \"Spread rests on N=1 (Qwen2.5-7B); No real-kernel latency benchmarks; untested beyond 14B.\"\n\n对于一篇存在以下重大限制的论文，这是不够的：\n1. Decision rule 的正样本仅 1 个（我的 R1-W1）\n2. 模型规模上限 14B（我的 R1-W4）\n3. Runtime 仅为 simulation（我的 R1-W6）\n4. 缺少 KVTuner 等直接 competitor 对比（我的 R1-W3）\n5. Downstream evaluation 无 confidence intervals（我的 R1-W5）\n\nACL ARR 要求 Limitations section 充分讨论方法的局限。当前版本远未达到标准。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-W8: Table caption 自包含性可改进**\n\n同意。Table 1 的 caption 需要参照正文 footnote 才能理解 \"standard-resolution\" vs \"high-resolution\" profiling 的区别。Table 4 的 t1/t5 定义在 caption 中过于简略（\"ratio of the most sensitive head's 2-bit distortion to the sum of the top-5% heads' distortions\"），不看正文很难理解。Minor 但按 EMNLP 标准应修正。\n\n---\n\n### Questions 回应\n\n**[AGREE] R2-Q1: Spread pattern 是模型固有属性还是校准数据的函数？**\n\n好问题。论文在 Appendix G 展示了 WikiText-2 vs C4 的 96-97% bit-assignment agreement，部分回答了这个问题。但这两个数据集都是 English web text，分布相似。如果用 code、multilingual、或 domain-specific 数据校准，sensitivity profile 是否改变？这直接影响 decision rule 的可靠性。论文应在 Discussion 中明确承认这一点。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE] R2-Q2: Profiling + k sweep + solver 的端到端开销是多少？**\n\n论文报告了 solver runtime（微秒级）但未报告 profiling 开销。Method.tex 第 25 行：\"64 sequences × 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train\"，H × |B| 次前向传播。对于 Qwen2.5-7B（112 heads × 4 bit-widths = 448 次前向传播），加上 k sweep，总计约 500+ 次前向传播。这是一个非 trivial 的计算成本，应当报告。\n\n---\n\n**[REBUT] R2-Q3: Yi-1.5 的 spike head 单独升级到 8-bit 是否能获益？**\n\n这个问题的答案已经隐含在论文中。Analysis.tex 第 18-19 行明确指出 Yi-1.5 的 L4H3 \"4-bit and 8-bit deltas are ≈ 0\"——即 d_h(4) ≈ d_h(8) ≈ 0。这意味着：\n\n1. 将 L4H3 从 4-bit 升级到 8-bit 不会减少任何 distortion（delta ≈ 0）\n2. 但会消耗额外 budget（4→8 bit 翻倍内存）\n3. 这正是 \"spike\" pattern 的定义特征：sensitivity 仅存在于 2-bit 维度，没有 cross-bitwidth gradient\n\n所以答案是：不能获益，因为该 head 的 4-bit distortion 已经 ≈ 0。Solver 在 4× 压缩下已经正确地将此 head 分配到 4-bit（而非 2-bit），这就是最优策略。进一步升级到 8-bit 只会浪费 budget 而无法降低 distortion。\n\n---\n\n**[AGREE，有补充] R2-Q4: Table 2 的 unconstrained MCKP 是否就是 RateQuant 复现？**\n\nMethod.tex 第 6-7 行明确说明 RateQuant 使用 {2,3,4,5,6}，本文使用 {2,4,8,16}。因此 unconstrained MCKP **不是** RateQuant 的精确复现——bit-width set 不同，polymatroid structure 不成立。\n\n但在精神上，R2 的观察成立：unconstrained MCKP 与 RateQuant 共享相同的优化框架（MCKP with additive distortion objective），只是应用于不同的 bit-width set。论文应在 Section 3.1 或 Table 1 caption 中更明确地说明这一关系，例如标注 \"Unconstrained MCKP (analogous to RateQuant adapted to {2,4,8,16})\"。\n\n---\n\n### 与我 R1 审稿意见的一致性总结\n\n| R2 观点 | R1 对应 | 一致性 |\n|---------|---------|--------|\n| W1 abstract 3 的效应量极小（±0.3-1.2%），在无 CI 的情况下无法判断显著性。",
